# three-virtual-geometry

> Virtual geometry for three.js WebGPU: a cluster level-of-detail hierarchy built per mesh, selected per frame on
> the GPU, with frustum, size and occlusion culling. Lets a scene hold billions of source triangles while drawing a
> few million. MIT license. Independent implementation, not affiliated with Epic Games.

Docs: https://elad12390.github.io/three-virtual-geometry/
Repository: https://github.com/elad12390/three-virtual-geometry
Package: three-virtual-geometry (npm). Peer dependency: three >= 0.180. Requires WebGPU (WebGPURenderer).

## Setup (the whole integration)

```ts
import * as THREE from 'three/webgpu';            // must be the WebGPU build of three.js
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';
import { VirtualGeometry } from 'three-virtual-geometry';

const renderer = new THREE.WebGPURenderer({ antialias: true });
await renderer.init();                            // required before rendering
const vg = new VirtualGeometry();                 // one per app

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('model.glb');
await vg.add(gltf.scene);                         // converts static meshes in place
scene.add(gltf.scene);

await vg.compileAsync(renderer, scene, camera);   // optional, during a loading screen
renderer.setAnimationLoop(() => renderer.render(scene, camera)); // unchanged render loop
```

Rules:
- Do not call vg.update() unless vg.autoUpdate was set to false; it runs automatically before each render.
- vg.add() keeps materials (converted to node materials), textures, shadows flags, names and userData. Skinned and
  morphing meshes, points, lines and sprites are left as normal three.js objects.
- Repeated geometry becomes one instanced VirtualMesh automatically. Builds are cached in IndexedDB.
- After moving an imported object, call result.syncTransforms() (result = return value of vg.add).
- To undo: result.dispose().
- In custom node materials use vgUv (not uv()) and vgWorldNormal.

## Without npm (CDN, plain HTML)

All-in-one build (contains three.js WebGPU build as THREE, TSL, GLTFLoader, OrbitControls, RoomEnvironment). Do not
load three.js a second time on the same page:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { THREE, VirtualGeometry, GLTFLoader, OrbitControls } from
    'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three-virtual-geometry@0.1/dist/three-virtual-geometry.all.min.js';
</script>
```

Minimal build (no three.js inside; needs an import map that comes before any module script):

```html
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
  "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.186.1/build/three.webgpu.js",
  "three/webgpu": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.186.1/build/three.webgpu.js",
  "three/tsl": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.186.1/build/three.tsl.js",
  "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.186.1/examples/jsm/",
  "three-virtual-geometry": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three-virtual-geometry@0.1/dist/three-virtual-geometry.min.js"
} }
</script>
```

Pages must be served over https or http://localhost (not file://). Full guide: https://elad12390.github.io/three-virtual-geometry/guide/cdn

## Geometry made in code

```ts
import { buildVirtualMeshCached, fromBufferGeometry } from 'three-virtual-geometry';
const data = await buildVirtualMeshCached(fromBufferGeometry(geometry));
const matrices = new Float32Array(16 * count);    // column-major Matrix4 per instance
for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) matrix.toArray(matrices, i * 16);
const mesh = vg.createMesh(data, new THREE.MeshStandardNodeMaterial({ color: 0x888888 }), { matrices });
scene.add(mesh);
mesh.setMatrixAt(0, newMatrix); mesh.commitInstances();          // move instances later
```

## Levers (all optional)

- new VirtualGeometry({ maxTriangles: 10_000_000, maxShadowTriangles: 4_000_000, maxMeshlets: 1 << 20 })
- vg.errorThreshold.value = 1          // pixels of error; higher = faster, coarser
- vg.triangleBudget = 0                // >0: adapt the threshold to this many triangles
- vg.minPixelRadius.value = 0.7        // skip instances smaller than this (pixels)
- vg.occlusion.enabled / vg.occlusion.auto
- vg.shadowErrorScale.value = 3
- mesh.maxDrawDistance = 400           // per mesh, e.g. grass; instances fade by shrinking
- vg.add(obj, { build: { prune: true }, mesh: { maxDrawDistance: 400 }, filter: m => true, onProgress })
- vg.debugMode.value = VG_DEBUG_MODES.meshlets

## Checking it works

const s = await vg.readStats(renderer);   // drawnTriangles << fullDetailTriangles, overflow === false

## Offline baking

npx vg-bake model.glb -o public/baked/model   -> *.vgeo + manifest.json; load with loadVirtualMesh(url).

## Limitations

Static meshes only (instances can move). One UV channel. Needs WebGPU (Chrome/Edge 113+, Safari 26+).
